📖 How to use

  1. Choose the conversion direction: binary → Gray or Gray → binary.
  2. Type the bit string (e.g. 10110) or switch to decimal input mode.
  3. Press Convert to see the result plus the XOR steps used.
  4. Check the 0–15 table to see the pattern: only one bit changes between neighbours.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What is Gray code?

Gray code (reflected binary code) orders binary values so consecutive numbers differ in exactly one bit. It is used in rotary encoders, Karnaugh maps and error-tolerant digital communication.

How is binary converted to Gray?

Keep the most significant bit, then each next Gray bit is the XOR of the current and previous binary bit: G = B XOR (B >> 1).

How is Gray converted back to binary?

Keep the most significant bit, then each binary bit is the XOR of the previous binary bit and the current Gray bit, cascading left to right.
